confirm.text: Nothing to report for 11/26. The "What did we observe?" multi-select appears only on the air job and OWL After Action Review forms, and no form of either kind was submitted on this date — the board shows every air job row on standby. None of the eight H2S dailies carries a multi-select field of any kind.

Air jobs. Nothing missing. The Permian board carries four air job rows on 11/26 — Fasken Oil & Ranch BV North Battery (two rows, AT# 501), SM Energy UL BOET (AT# 504) and SM Energy Earl Hankammer CTB (AT# 507, noted on the board as "SHUTTING DOWN 11/26-11/28"). All four show ON STANDBY in the technician columns, so there is no assignment on any of them and no job submission, Trailer Inspection Form or Trailer Readiness Form is owed. This is why no trailer forms of either kind appear for 11/26, and it is expected rather than a gap. The ArkLaTex board carries no air job rows.
Confined space. Neither board carries a confined space row on 11/26.
Supervision. Three assigned shifts have no H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form in the mailbox as of this run:

Michael Ellis — Comstock, Kern PP 1H, drillout, supervision (nights), ticket 95222, AT# 103. The day shift on this row, Josh Blassingame, filed at 9:23 AM. No night form from Ellis was received. He is a full-time employee and the board shows him working and scheduled for nights, so this is the one to check first. Night-shift forms routinely arrive late in the evening or the following morning — Allen White's night form for 11/26 did not land until 9:26 PM — and this run started before the day closed, so this may well resolve on its own overnight.
Brynn Taylor 1099 — SM Energy, Scott State Afterbuzz E 143H, workover, supervision (days), ticket 103111, AT# 151. No form received.
Eddy Hadaway 1099 — SM Energy, Seinfeld Fed Unit Mulva 133H, workover, supervision (days), ticket 103118, AT# 148. No form received.

Both Brynn Taylor and Eddy Hadaway are 1099 contractors. It is still not established whether every 1099 contractor is set up to file in StreetSmart at all, so a form that was never expected is not a form that is missing. These two are listed for confirmation rather than as confirmed failures.
Field service. Neither board carries a field service row on 11/26, and no field service forms were submitted.

Satisfied in ways that may look wrong at a glance. Larry Taylor's assignment is the Comstock drilling EIR inspection route, which the board lists as "MULTIPLE LOCATIONS" with AT# N/A; his form names the specific site, Neyland (904), so it was matched to the board by technician name rather than location, and his documentation is present. The complete absence of Trailer Inspection Forms and Trailer Readiness Forms on 11/26 is correct, not an omission, because every air job row was on standby. Gate guard, traffic control and HSE/safety rows on the ArkLaTex board are all 1099 assignments and are grouped with the contractors above.

doc.text: Bottle Hydro Dates and cascade pressures

Brey Rasco, Mitsui E&P, Lipsey 1H, 12:51 PM — both "Pressure on Cascade System" and "Bottle Hydro Dates" are blank. The board shows AT# 140 on this row, so a trailer is on location and both fields were expected. Re-read from the source PDF: the entry runs "10.2. 11.1. 10.7. 11.5. 11.2. 11.2. 10.7. 11.2 Sensor Battery Levels Pressure on Cascade System Bottle Hydro Dates" — the single value belongs to Sensor Battery Levels and the other two fields carry nothing. This is the one valid hydro and cascade finding for the day.

Clean on both fields: Allen White (trailer 140, "8@2300" and "8@3-23"), Dennis Easley (trailer 505, "2@1000psi 4@2000psi" and "6@4/23"), Justin Pack (trailer 505, "3@2000,1000,2@2400" and "6@4/23"), Joshua Blassingame (trailer 103, "All bottles full" and "3-23").

Exempt because the board AT# is exactly "N/A", meaning no air trailer on location: Larry Taylor (Comstock inspection route) and 1099 Benjamin Boutte (Ovintiv, St Elmo, H&P 616). Both left these fields blank and both are correct to have done so. Boutte has filed blank cascade and hydro fields on previous days where a trailer was present, so this is worth noting for continuity — but on 11/26 there is nothing for him to correct.
1099 Marcos Morales — not assessed, PDF unreadable. His row is also AT# N/A.
Photos not taken on the day being verified

Joshua Blassingame, Comstock Resources, Kern PP 1H, 9:23 AM — the ELSA photo and the Loud Alarm Position photo are both stamped 08/12/2021 10:02 AM, over five years before the form date. Four gas monitor photos are stamped 11/18/2026 09:25 AM, eight days stale: three under "Picture of Front and Back of 4 Gas With Pump" and one under "Picture of Front and Back of Single Gas/4 Gas Without Pump". Every other photo on the form is same-day.
Allen White, MEP, Lipsey 1-H, 9:20 PM — the ELSA photo is stamped 08/12/2021 10:02 AM. It is the only photo on his form not dated 11/26.
Larry Taylor, Comstock, Neyland (904), 3:37 PM — the four gas monitor photos are stamped 11/25/2026, 4:24 and 4:25 PM, the previous afternoon. All other photos on the form are same-day.

Worth a closer look: White's ELSA photo and both of Blassingame's stale photos carry the identical capture stamp of 08/12/2021 10:02 AM, on forms filed by different technicians for different customers at different locations. That pattern suggests one stale image being reused across the region rather than two separate oversights, but it needs confirmation before anyone treats it as established.
Stale ELSA and Loud Alarm Position photos on the H2S daily remain the most persistent documentation problem in this review.

clean.text: Dennis Easley filed an H2S Safety Supervision Daily Inspection Form for Southwest Operations, Hughes #1, with both cascade and hydro fields populated, the complete air-trailer photo set, and every photo on the form captured on 11/26. Justin Pack filed the day-shift H2S daily on the same job with the same completeness — the most fully documented form in the set. 1099 Benjamin Boutte filed an H2S daily for Ovintiv, St Elmo, with every photo captured same-day; his blank cascade and hydro fields and empty trailer photo sections are correct for a row with no air trailer assigned. Nothing on any of these three requires attention.

Trailer forms of both kinds and the equipment sections of the H2S daily are photo-based, so a defect visible only in a photograph would not surface in this review. Fire extinguisher inspection and expiration dates, first aid kit dates and 4-gas calibration dates exist only inside images, not as text, so they cannot be read or checked here.

A second limitation applies to this run specifically. The H2S daily filed by 1099 Marcos Morales at 4:44 PM is a 30 MB PDF, which exceeds the 26 MB limit for reading an attachment through the mail connector. It was attempted twice and could not be opened. That form is counted as a submission and as an assignment satisfied, but none of its content has been reviewed — not the FR answer, not the cascade and hydro fields, not the photo dates. It needs to be opened directly in Outlook.

9 of 10 submissions read. The job board was available: the 11/26/2026 board email from Blake Walton arrived at 10:37 AM and both the ArkLaTex and Permian Basin November 2026 workbooks were read from the 11-26 sheet. 45 manned board rows were checked for coverage, 16 on the ArkLaTex board and 29 on the Permian board. This run started at 11:06 PM Central, before the Central day closed, so any form submitted in the final hour of 11/26 is not in these counts — and night-shift forms in particular often arrive hours late or the following morning, which is the most likely resolution for the missing Michael Ellis daily.
